"Hajj is Arafat" — this hadith highlights the central role of Arafat in Hajj.
"I would owe fasts from Ramadan and I could not make them up except in Shaban."
"Indeed, it is We who revealed the Quran and indeed, We will be its Guardian."
"La ilaha illallah" — foundation of Islam, key to Paradise, the weightiest word
"That used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fasts but not commanded to make up the prayers."
"When you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break your fast. If it is hidden from you by clouds, then fast thirty days."
"Whoever among you is ill or on a journey — then an equal number of other days."
"Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected."
"Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, its expiation is to pray it when he remembers it."
(O Allah), I ask You for Your forgiveness.
40 Hadith — No. 19: “Young man, guard Allah…”
A blessed Book which We have revealed to you, that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded.
A cheerful face and a good word (at-Tirmidhi 1956; Muslim 2626; al-Bukhari 2989).
A dua is never wasted: either what is asked is given, or an evil is turned away.

After the tashahhud, “let him choose whichever dua he likes and make it” (al-Bukhari 835). Asked which dua is most heard: “In the last part of the night and at the end of the obligatory prayers” (at-Tirmidhi 3499, hasan).
All greetings, prayers and good deeds are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.

Allah created Adam and taught him the names of all things. He commanded the angels to prostrate to him — they all did, except Iblis, who refused out of arrogance. Adam and his wife lived in Paradise, and Allah forbade them to approach one tree. Satan tricked them and they slipped. Adam received words from his Lord and repented, and Allah accepted his repentance.

Allah had taught Sulayman the language of birds. One day he came with his army to the valley of the ants. An ant said: “O ants, enter your homes so that Sulayman and his army do not crush you without noticing!” Sulayman smiled at her words and prayed: “My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour upon me and my parents, and to do good deeds that please You.”
Allah has 99 names — whoever memorizes them will enter Paradise.
Allah helps His servant as long as the servant helps his brother.

Allah inspired Musa’s mother: “Nurse him, and when you fear for him, put him in the river; do not fear or grieve — We will return him to you.” Pharaoh’s family picked the baby out of the water, but Allah returned him to his mother so she would know that Allah’s promise is true. Years later Pharaoh and his army chased the believers to the sea. Musa said: “No! My Lord is with me; He will guide me.” Allah said: “Strike the sea with your staff” — and it parted, and the believers were saved.

Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are [only] daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one’s estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one’s parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents [alone] inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents or your children — you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. [These shares are] an obligation [imposed] by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
Allahumma inni as’aluka min fadlik
Allahumma-ftah li abwaba rahmatik

Among the deeds and good works that reach a believer after his death are: knowledge he taught and spread, a righteous child he left behind, a copy of the Quran he bequeathed, a mosque he built, a house he built for travellers, a stream he made flow, or charity he gave from his wealth while healthy and alive — these reach him after his death.
And We have certainly made the Quran easy to remember. So is there anyone who will be mindful?
And establish prayer for My remembrance.

And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for the wives is one fourth if you leave no child. But if you leave a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third, after any bequest which was made or debt, as long as there is no detriment [caused]. [This is] an ordinance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
And indeed it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners — in a clear Arabic tongue.
And seek help through patience and prayer.
And when My servants ask you about Me — indeed I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me.

As a boy, Yusuf saw in a dream eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him. His father Yaqub told him not to tell his brothers. Out of jealousy the brothers harmed him, and Yusuf was patient for many years. In the end Allah raised him high. When his brothers came, he did not take revenge, but said: “No blame upon you today. May Allah forgive you!”
Beneficial knowledge is one of the three deeds whose reward continues after death (Muslim 1631).

Both legal and illegal things are evident but in between them there are doubtful (suspicious) things and most of the people have no knowledge about them. So whoever saves himself from these suspicious things saves his religion and his honor. And whoever indulges in these suspicious things is like a shepherd who grazes (his animals) near the Hima (private pasture) of someone else and at any moment he is liable to get in it…
Charity does not decrease wealth.
Command your children to pray when they are seven, discipline them for it when they are ten, and separate them in their beds.
Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face.
Do not pass between a person praying and his sutrah (a wall, pillar or object); pass behind him or at a sufficient distance.
Do not think little of a small gift
Dots distinguish letters from one another (ب ت ث; ج ح خ). There are no vowel signs yet.
Dua is worship itself. (Then he recited: “Your Lord has said: Call upon Me; I will respond to you” — Ghafir 40:60.)
Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. (The hadith continues: a man is the shepherd of his family, and a woman is the shepherd of her husband’s house and children.)
Establish prayer and give zakat
Establish prayer, give zakah, and bow with those who bow.
Even saying “be quiet” to your companion while the imam is speaking is idle talk.
Every act of kindness is charity.
Every day two angels descend; one says: "O Allah, give the spender a replacement," and the other says: "O Allah, give the miser destruction."

Every joint of a person owes charity every day the sun rises: judging justly between two people is charity; helping a man onto his mount or lifting his luggage onto it is charity; a good word is charity; every step you take to the prayer is charity; and removing harm from the path is charity.
Every tasbih, takbir, tahmid and tahlil is charity (Muslim 1006). When you pray for your brother in his absence, an angel says: “And for you the same” (Muslim 2732).
Glory be to You O Allah, and praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, there is no god but You.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, for we could never have done it ourselves; and to our Lord we will surely return.
Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devout obedience.

He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
He is not of us who does not recite the Quran in a pleasant tone.
He neither begot nor was begotten — nothing resembles Him, none equals Him

Ibn Umar said: “While the people were at Quba in the Fajr prayer, someone came to them and said: ‘Quran has been revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ tonight and he has been commanded to face the Kaaba, so face it.’ Their faces were towards Sham, and they turned round towards the Kaaba.”
Ibn Umar: “When travelling, the Prophet ﷺ prayed the night prayer on his mount, wherever it took him, making gestures — except the obligatory prayers — and he prayed witr on his mount.”
Ibn Uthaymin: “Enumerating them means memorising their words and understanding their meaning, and its completion is worshipping Allah according to what they require” (al-Qawa‘id al-Muthla).

Ibrahim, together with his son Ismail, raised the foundations of the House (the Kaaba). While working they made dua: “Our Lord, accept this from us! You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Make us Muslims, submitting to You.”

Ibrahim’s people worshipped idols made of stone. He broke the idols, leaving only the biggest one. When they questioned him, he said: “Ask them, if they can speak!” They realised that the idols could not speak, benefit or harm. Even so, they threw Ibrahim into a fire. Allah said: “O fire, be coolness and safety for Ibrahim!”
In Rabi‘ al-Awwal, on a Monday, they reached Quba, the quarter of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. The Prophet ﷺ stayed there some ten-odd nights and founded the mosque built on taqwa.
In every difficulty we turn to Allah in dua. Allah says: “And thus do We save the believers.”
In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
In the cave of Hira the opening verses of al-‘Alaq — “Read in the name of your Lord who created…” — were revealed. (Bukhari 3)
In the name of Allah, I rely upon Allah. There is no might and no power except with Allah.
In the name of Allah. Eat with your right hand and from what is in front of you.
Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian.
Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at fixed times.
Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.
Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, Hajj and fasting Ramadan.
It is He who created for you all of that which is on the earth. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, [His being above all creation], and made them seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.
It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases — that you may know the number of years and account [of time].
It is prayed as soon as one remembers or wakes up — there is no other expiation for it.
It will be said to the companion of the Quran: “Recite and rise, and recite slowly as you used to in the world, for your rank is at the last verse you recite.”
Jabir ibn Abdullah: “The Prophet ﷺ used to pray voluntary prayers while riding, facing other than the qibla.”
Jabir: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on his mount wherever it faced; when he wanted to pray the obligatory prayer he dismounted and faced the qibla.”
Keep revising the Quran! By Him in whose hand is my soul, it escapes faster than camels from their hobbles.

LIMITLESS in His glory is He who transported His servant by night from the Inviolable House of Worship [at Mecca] to the Remote House of Worship [, at Jerusalem] - the environs of which We had blessed -so that We might show him some of Our symbols: for, verily, He alone is all-hearing, all-seeing.
La ilaha illallah — none has the right to be worshipped but Allah
Luqman’s first advice to his son: “O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, shirk is a great injustice” (Luqman 31:13).

Maryam brought the baby Isa to her people, and they blamed her. She pointed to the baby. They said: “How can we speak to a child in the cradle?” Then Isa spoke: “I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah as long as I live, and to be dutiful to my mother.”
May Allah reward you with good. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever says this has praised in the fullest way.
My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small.
My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
Never will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. And whatever you spend — Allah knows it.

Nuh called his people for a long time to worship Allah alone, but only a few believed. By Allah’s command he built a ship. When the flood began, the believers boarded saying “In the name of Allah”. Nuh called his son too, but the son said: “I will take refuge on a mountain.” Nuh said: “Today there is no protector from Allah’s decree, except for whom He has mercy.” Then the water went down and the ship came to rest on Mount Judi.
O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female devils.
O Allah, bring it upon us with blessing, faith, safety and Islam. (O moon,) my Lord and your Lord is Allah.
O Allah, in Your name I die and I live.
O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim.
O you who believe, when the call is made for the prayer on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade.
O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire…

Of a man who made dua without praising Allah or sending salawat, the Prophet ﷺ said: “He was hasty,” and taught: first praise and glorify your Lord, then send salawat on the Prophet, then ask for what you wish (Abu Dawud 1481, sahih).
Of the dinars spent in Allah’s cause, on freeing a slave, on a poor person and on one’s family, the greatest in reward is the one spent on one’s family (Muslim 995).
On Friday there is a moment: no Muslim servant standing in prayer asks Allah for something in it but He gives it to him.
On Friday there is an hour in which no Muslim servant stands in prayer asking Allah for something but that He gives it to him (al-Bukhari 935; Muslim 852).
On entering: “O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.”
On leaving: “O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.”
One Umrah to the next is an expiation for what is between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise.
One prayer performed here is superior to one thousand prayers in other mosques (except Masjid al-Haram).
Our Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains and says: “Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him?” (al-Bukhari 1145; Muslim 758).
Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire (al-Baqarah 2:201).
Performing two rak'ahs of prayer here earns the reward of an Umrah.
Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to find a way to it.
Planting a tree — if a bird, person or animal eats from it, it is charity (al-Bukhari 2320; Muslim 1553).
Praise be to Allah who clothed me with this garment and provided it for me without any might or power from me.
Praise be to Allah who fed me this food and provided it for me without any might or power from me.
Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the return.
Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date.
Purity is half of faith.
Recite the Quran, for on the Day of Resurrection it will come as an intercessor for its companions.
Removing harm from the path is charity.
Right after worshipping Him, Allah commands kindness to parents.
Send abundant salawat upon me on Friday.

Seven will be shaded by Allah in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His… (among them) a man who gives charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives.
So when the Quran is recited, listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy.
Spreading salam makes us love one another.
Straighten the rows and stand close together
Straighten your rows, for straightening the rows is part of establishing the prayer properly.
Successful indeed are the believers — those who are humble in their prayer.
The Prophet ﷺ did not fast in any month, other than Ramadan, as much as he fasted in Sha‘ban (al-Bukhari 1969).
The Prophet ﷺ gently told the boy in his care: “Young boy, mention Allah’s name, eat with your right hand and eat from what is in front of you” (al-Bukhari 5376).
The Prophet ﷺ kissed his grandson al-Hasan; to a man who said he had never kissed any of his ten children he said: “Whoever shows no mercy will be shown no mercy” (al-Bukhari 5997).

The Prophet ﷺ loved to begin with the right in all his affairs (al-Bukhari 426). On this basis scholars consider it recommended to enter the mosque with the right foot and leave with the left. On entering and leaving one says the duas the Prophet ﷺ taught:
The Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man on a long journey, dishevelled, raising his hands to the sky: “O Lord, O Lord” — while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful: how can he be answered? (Muslim 1015).
The Prophet ﷺ said he was about to burn the houses of men who stayed away from the congregation (Bukhari 644), and that the heaviest prayers for the hypocrites are Fajr and Isha (Bukhari 657).
The Prophet ﷺ said: “No prayer is heavier upon the hypocrites than Fajr and ‘Isha.” Forty days is simply a period chosen to build a habit — we do not attach any special virtue to the number.
The Prophet’s ﷺ ‘umrahs, other than the one with his Hajj, were in this month (al-Bukhari 1778)
The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
The charity with the greatest reward is given while you are healthy, attached to wealth, fearing poverty and hoping for riches — do not delay until the soul reaches the throat (al-Bukhari 1419).
The days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking and remembering Allah — one does not fast on them (Muslim 1141).
The most beloved deeds are the most constant, even if small (al-Bukhari 6464, Muslim 782).
The most beloved deeds are those done consistently, even if small (Bukhari 6464).
The one who is skilled in the Quran is with the noble, righteous scribes (angels); and the one who recites it haltingly, finding it hard, has two rewards.

The one who sneezes says “Alhamdulillah”; the listener says “Yarhamuk-Allah” (may Allah have mercy on you); and the sneezer replies “Yahdikumullahu wa yuslihu balakum” (may Allah guide you and set your affairs right).
The same prayer, a different reward: prayer in congregation surpasses praying alone by twenty-seven degrees.
The skeleton of the letters: no dots, no vowel signs. Several letters share one shape — inside a word ب ت ث ن ي are the same “tooth”.

There is no Muslim on earth who calls upon Allah with a dua except that Allah gives it to him or turns away from him an equal evil — as long as he does not pray for sin or for cutting family ties. A man said: “Then we will pray a lot.” He ﷺ said: “Allah is more (generous).”
There is reward for kindness to every living creature.

They request from you a [legal] ruling. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling concerning one having neither descendants nor ascendants [as heirs].” If a man dies, leaving no child but [only] a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits from her if she [dies and] has no child. But if there are two sisters [or more], they will have two-thirds of what he left. If there are both brothers and sisters, the male will have the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you [His law], lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
To a Companion who gave a gift to one son but not the others, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Fear Allah and be just between your children” — and he took the gift back (al-Bukhari 2587; Muslim 1623).
To the one who asked for advice the Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not get angry.”
Travel for worship only to three mosques
Truthfulness leads to goodness, and goodness leads to Paradise.
Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest.
Verily, with every hardship comes ease.
Voluntary prayers before and after the obligatory ones. Whoever prays 12 rak‘ahs a day, a house is built for him in Paradise (Muslim 728).
We worship Allah alone — no one else can benefit or harm.
When Banu Salimah wanted to move close to the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Stay in your homes; your footsteps are being written” (Muslim 665).

When Umar asked how to use his most precious land at Khaybar, the Prophet ﷺ said: “If you wish, keep its origin (as an endowment) and give its yield in charity.” Umar made it an endowment that could not be sold, gifted or inherited; its yield went to the poor, relatives, the cause of Allah, travellers and guests.
When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: … or a righteous child who prays for him.
When a person dies, his deeds end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.

When the Prophet ﷺ fasted Ashura he was told that the Jews and Christians venerate this day. He said: “Next year, if Allah wills, we will fast the ninth day” (Muslim 1134). So Tasu‘a is fasted together with Ashura.
When the Prophet ﷺ sent Muʿadh to Yemen he said: “…teach them that Allah has made zakat obligatory on their wealth: it is taken from their rich and given to their poor.”
When the Quran is recited, stop talking and listen attentively.

When the qibla was changed, the people of Quba were in the Fajr prayer. When the news reached them, they turned towards the Kaaba without breaking their prayer and completed it. Scholars infer from this that whoever learns the correct direction during the prayer turns and continues.
When you recite the Quran, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled.
While the Prophet ﷺ was giving the khutbah a man came in and sat. He asked: “Have you prayed?” — “No.” — “Then pray two rak‘ahs” (al-Bukhari 931, Muslim 875). These two rak‘ahs are kept light.
Who comes in the first hour is like one who offered a camel; when the imam comes out, the angels come to listen to the reminder.
Whoever fears Allah and is patient — Allah does not let the reward of the good-doers be lost. Forgiving is beautiful.
Whoever gives a date's worth of charity from pure earnings, Allah accepts it with His right hand.

Whoever goes in the first hour is like one who offered a camel, in the second a cow, in the third a horned ram, in the fourth a hen, in the fifth an egg; when the imam comes out, the angels come to listen to the reminder (al-Bukhari 881).
Whoever memorizes them enters Paradise
Whoever performs Hajj for Allah and does not commit obscenity or sin returns like the day his mother bore him.
Whoever reads Surah al-Kahf on Friday, light will illuminate for him between the two Fridays.

Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah receives a good deed, and a good deed is multiplied ten times. I do not say that “Alif-Lam-Mim” is one letter; rather Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter.
Whoever recites them is protected from illness
Whoever writes them earns reward
Your smile in your brother’s face is charity for you.

Your smile in your brother’s face is charity for you; enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity; guiding a man who is lost is charity; seeing for a man with poor sight is charity; removing a stone, a thorn or a bone from the path is charity; and pouring from your bucket into your brother’s bucket is charity.

Yunus left his people in anger and boarded a laden ship. Then a big fish swallowed him. In the darkness he called on Allah: “There is no god but You. Glory be to You! I have been among the wrongdoers.” Allah answered him, saved him from distress, cast him onto the shore and made a plant grow over him.

‘Abdullah ibn as-Sa’ib said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say between the two Corners…” (Abu Dawud 1892; graded hasan by al-Albani in Sahih Abi Dawud).
“Call upon Allah while certain of being answered, and know that Allah does not answer the dua of a heedless, distracted heart” (at-Tirmidhi 3479, hasan).
“Call upon your Lord humbly and privately” (al-A‘raf 7:55). “Your Lord is Shy and Generous: He is shy, when His servant raises his hands to Him, to return them empty” (Abu Dawud 1488, sahih).
“Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah.”
“Do not prevent your women from the mosques, but their houses are better for them.”
“Dua made between the adhan and the iqamah is not rejected” (Abu Dawud 521, sahih).
“Ghusl on Friday is obligatory for everyone who has reached puberty, and that he cleans his teeth with siwak and applies perfume if he finds any” (al-Bukhari 880).
“Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness of complete light on the Day of Resurrection.”
“Give the fixed shares to those entitled to them, and whatever remains goes to the nearest male relative.”

“If the one who passes in front of a person praying knew what (sin) is upon him, it would be better for him to stand still for forty than to pass in front of him.” (The narrator was unsure whether he said forty days, months or years.)
“If you say to your companion ‘Be quiet’ on Friday while the imam is speaking, you have engaged in idle talk” (al-Bukhari 934). Busying yourself with a phone or chatting falls under the same.

“Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve in the Book of Allah, on the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the upright religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them.”
“None of you should say: ‘O Allah, forgive me if You wish.’ Let him be resolute in his asking, for no one can compel Allah” (al-Bukhari 6339; Muslim 2679).
“N” to true north (not magnetic north)
“O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury” (al-Baqarah 2:264). Exposing the recipient’s identity, photo or name is also a form of this injury.
“Read the Qur’an in a month.” Abdullah said: “I find myself able to do more.” He ﷺ said: “Then read it in seven days and do not go beyond that.”
“Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.”

“Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday, for your blessings are presented to me” (Abu Dawud 1047, sahih). On this day there is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks Allah for something but He gives it to him (al-Bukhari 935).

“Shall I not tell you of that by which Allah erases sins and raises degrees?” — “Performing ablution thoroughly despite difficulties, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the next prayer after a prayer. That is the ribat” (Muslim 251).
“Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account.”
“The Message of the Qur’an” — English translation of the meaning
“The believer keeps watch over himself; he takes account of himself for the sake of Allah.”
“The best dua is the dua of the Day of Arafah” (at-Tirmidhi 3585, hasan).
“The closest a servant is to his Lord is while prostrating, so make much dua then” (Muslim 482).

“The days of Tashreeq are days of eating and drinking” (Muslim 1141) — and days of remembering Allah and takbir. Fasting in them is not permitted, except for a pilgrim who could not find a sacrificial animal (al-Bukhari 1997).
“The dua of each of you is answered as long as he is not hasty, saying: ‘I prayed but was not answered’” (al-Bukhari 6340; Muslim 2735). Your journal helps you stay patient.
“The people with the greatest reward for prayer are those who walk the farthest distance (to it).”

“The upper (giving) hand is better than the lower hand; begin with those you support. The best charity is given out of surplus” (al-Bukhari 1427). Charity to a relative has two rewards: for kinship and for charity (al-Bukhari 1466). The verse also puts parents and relatives first (al-Baqarah 2:215).
“The year is twelve months, four of which are sacred: three in succession — Dhul-Qa‘dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram — and the Rajab of Mudar, which comes between Jumada and Sha‘ban.”
“Three duas are answered without doubt: the dua of a parent, the dua of a traveller and the dua of the oppressed” (Abu Dawud 1536, hasan).
“We are an unlettered nation; we do not write or calculate. The month is like this and like this” — meaning sometimes twenty-nine and sometimes thirty days.

“We have seen the turning of your face towards the heaven. So We will surely turn you to a qibla with which you will be pleased. So turn your face towards al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it. Those who were given the Scripture know well that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.”
“What is between the east and the west is qibla.”
“When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath.”
“When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rak‘ahs before sitting.”
“When one of you has prayed the Friday prayer, let him pray four after it.”
“When one of you prays Jumu‘ah, let him pray four (rak‘ahs) after it” (Muslim 881).
“When one of you prays towards something that screens him from people (a sutrah) and someone wants to pass in front of him, let him push him back.”
“When you stand for prayer, perform ablution thoroughly, then face the qibla and say the takbir…”
“Whoever eats from this foul-smelling plant should not come near our mosque, for the angels are harmed by what harms human beings.”
“Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime” (Muslim 1164). The six days may be any days of Shawwal after Eid.
“Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning and the evening, Allah prepares for him a place of hospitality in Paradise every time he goes, morning or evening.”
“Whoever has eaten garlic or onion, let him keep away from us — or he said: from our mosque — and stay in his house.”
“Whoever introduces into this matter of ours (the religion) something that is not part of it, it is rejected.”
“Whoever purifies himself in his house, then walks to one of the houses of Allah to fulfil one of the obligations of Allah, one of his steps removes a sin and the other raises him a degree.”
“Whoever raises two girls until they reach maturity, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like this” — and he joined his fingers (Muslim 2631).
…And recite the Quran with measured recitation.
